_comment: Which tool is a Hermes approval prompt about? Hermes carries no structured tool field on an approval event, so the name has to be parsed back out of two strings it does carry. Three consumers need the answer — the audit log (hermes/plugins/_shared/_approval_hook.tool_from_approval), the benchmark's approval_gate checker (bench/checkers.py) and the console's approval card (aura-web/src/lib/hermes/approvalEvent.ts) — and they are in two languages, so the cases live here rather than in either. Python reads this in hermes/plugins/tests/test_approval_event.py; TypeScript in aura-web/src/lib/hermes/approvalEvent.test.ts. The prose is hermes/plugins/_shared/_approval_event.py's module docstring.

ask_why._comment: T-1054. 'Ask why' on an approval card is a deny first: Hermes's approval.respond carries no text, so the question goes out as the next prompt.submit, after the no. Only a Hermes approval offers it (never the phone's own Tier-3 asks, never a phone-confirmed one on the console), and it is enabled whenever Deny is. The countdown's auto-deny never sends it. The console (aura-web/src/lib/ds/shell/approval.ts) and the phone (ui/ApprovalBridge.kt) both build the line from this template; {what} is the card's headline cut to what_cap characters, {why} is the sentence.
ask_why.sentence: Before asking again, say why you need this.
ask_why.template: You asked: “{what}”. I said no for now. {why}

card._comment: T-0606: an approval is one clear ask. Hermes' request_tool_approval has no slot but the reason string, so the card travels as the LAST FIVE LINES of the reason (hermes/plugins/_shared/_messages.card writes them, parse_card reads them; aura-web/src/lib/hud/approvalCard.ts is the console's parser). Anything before them stays what it was: the first-message and outside-read prefixes come first, then the rule sentence. A reason without the five lines parses to null and the app shows the plain reason. Undoable no = hold to confirm. Home yes = the owner is home now, so the 'when I'm home' chip may be offered. The chips map onto Hermes' choices; 'Show me first' answers nothing and only reveals the arguments, which are in the sentence above the card.

change._comment: T-1317, T-1329: an approval to change a setting, the chat's model, a device's name or a model's launch settings shows the value now and the value it would become. The approval has no slot but the reason string, so the gate (hermes/plugins/_shared/_approval_hook.matrix_gate, told by the settings plugin's change_for) writes three one-line fields DIRECTLY BEFORE the five card lines (_messages.change writes them, parse_change reads them; aura-web/src/lib/hud/approvalCard.ts parseApprovalChange is the console's parser). The console draws rows from them only for the tools named here; anywhere else, or anywhere but directly before a card, the three lines are prose. A secret's two values are both the mask, set or not, and the app then says only that it changes. A consumer that does not know the lines shows them as text: the phone lists them under the card's details. Python reads this in hermes/plugins/aura-settings/tests/test_aura_settings.py; TypeScript in aura-web/src/lib/hud/approvalCard.test.ts.

phone_confirmation._comment: T-0945. A sensitive call is not put to Hermes' approval queue: the approval gate asks the adapter (POST /api/approval/proof), which shows it on every app as an approval.request with the fields below (request ids start proof-) and says yes only when approval.respond carries signature: base64 DER ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 over the challenge's UTF-8 bytes, by a key a paired phone registered. Every app then gets approval.resolved for that request id. The adapter reads this in aura-adapter/tests/test_approval_proof.py; each app's approval card binds the field names in its own suite.
phone_confirmation.challenge_shown: sha256 hex of json.dumps([command, description]) with Python's default separators (T-1030); an app signs the challenge as given and never rebuilds it
